---
title: "GitHub Codespaces — Quick reference"
---

This page collects the routine Codespaces operations used during the Mineral
Science laboratory.

## Open or resume the workspace

Open your private workspace repository and select:

**Code → Codespaces**

If an existing Codespace is listed, reopen it rather than creating a new one.

You can also manage all your Codespaces at:

<https://github.com/codespaces>

## Recommended resource settings

For this course, a **2-core** Codespace is sufficient.

If you need to check or change the current machine, open
<https://github.com/codespaces>, select the **...** menu for the Codespace and
choose **Change machine type**.

A **15-minute idle timeout** is recommended in your GitHub
**Settings → Codespaces**. This is a safety measure; you should still stop the
Codespace manually when finished.

## First launch is slower

Creating a Codespace for the first time requires GitHub to create the virtual
machine, configure the development container and install the scientific Python
environment.

Wait for:

```text
Environment ready.
```

Restarting the same stopped Codespace is normally much faster.

## Upload a file

Drag a local file into the required folder in the Explorer.

For course work, upload files into the appropriate directory under `work/`
unless the laboratory instructions explicitly state otherwise.

## Download a file

Right-click the file in the Explorer and select **Download**.

## Open a terminal

Use:

**Terminal → New Terminal**

Useful checks include:

```bash
pwd
ls
python --version
```

## Update distributed material

```bash
update-course
```

## Start a laboratory

```bash
start-lab 01
```

Replace `01` with the laboratory number.

## Save work to GitHub

Use the Source Control panel:

```text
stage → commit → Sync Changes
```

Remember that saving a notebook does not automatically send it to GitHub.

## Stop the Codespace

Preferred browser method:

<https://github.com/codespaces>

then:

**... → Stop codespace**

Alternative from inside the Codespace:

**Command Palette → Codespaces: Stop Current Codespace**

Closing the browser tab alone does not stop the Codespace.

## Delete a Codespace

Deleting a Codespace is **not** part of the normal end-of-session workflow.

Only delete it after confirming that all work you need has been committed and
synchronized to GitHub.

## Common problems

### The first launch appears to be doing nothing

Wait for the setup terminal to finish. Package installation during the first
creation can take several minutes.

### Python cannot import a course package

Make sure the initial setup has completed. If the problem remains, keep the
complete error message and contact the instructor rather than installing
different package versions manually.

### `update-course` reports an error

Do not delete or overwrite `work/`. Save and synchronize your current work, then
report the exact terminal message.

### Source Control says `Publish Branch`

Check that you created a private repository from the template **before**
creating the Codespace. A Codespace opened directly from the template is not
the intended course workflow.

### The Codespace is still running after I closed the tab

This is expected. Closing the web editor does not stop the remote machine.
Open <https://github.com/codespaces> and stop it explicitly.

## Official documentation

GitHub maintains current documentation at:

<https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces>
